claim: Nanning fell on 24 November 1939 and the Japanese evacuated it on 28 October 1940; the Kunlun Pass battle (18 December 1939 to 11 January 1940) was a Chinese victory
source: Wikipedia, Battle of South Guangxi; Wikipedia, Battle of Kunlun Pass
note: The zone is 'contested' from 1 January 1940 to 28 October 1940 on this basis.

claim: Ichi-Go opened on 17 April 1944 (some sources say 19 April); Guilin fell on 10 November 1944; the Japanese reached French Indochina in December 1944
source: Wikipedia, Operation Ichi-Go; Wikipedia, Battle of Hengyang
note: Liuzhou's fall is put on the same date as Guilin's (10 November 1944) without a source of its own; the retaking of Nanning (26 May 1945) is from memory.

claim: Nanning is retaken on 26 May 1945 (the Second Guangxi campaign, April to August 1945); the Japanese 58th Division left Liuzhou on 19 June; the zone is contested from 26 May to 15 August 1945
source: Wikipedia, Second Guangxi campaign; Wikipedia, 58th Division (Imperial Japanese Army)
note: Guilin's retaking (28 July) is from memory.

claim: Tarakan was attacked on 11 January 1942 and surrendered on 12 January; Balikpapan fell on 23 to 25 January 1942
source: Wikipedia, Dutch East Indies campaign; Wikipedia, Battle of Balikpapan (1942)
note: The zone turns 'axis' on 1 March 1942 as a round figure for the fall of Banjarmasin and Pontianak (February 1942); those dates are from memory.

claim: Palembang was taken by paratroops and landings on 13 to 16 February 1942 (the zone turns contested on the 14th); the Dutch on Sumatra capitulate on 28 March 1942
note: 28 March for Sumatra is from memory.

claim: The Battle of the Java Sea is on 27 February 1942 and the Dutch capitulate on 9 March 1942 (Kalijati)
source: From memory of the standard histories

claim: Manado is invaded on 11 January 1942 and Makassar falls on 9 February 1942
source: From memory of the standard histories

claim: Ambon is invaded on 30 to 31 January 1942; the zone is 'axis' from 19 April 1942 (Hollandia taken); the American landing at Hollandia is on 22 April 1944
source: From memory of the standard histories
note: Check before release; the Japanese landings in West New Guinea were on several dates in April 1942.

claim: Luzon is contested from 8 December 1941; Corregidor surrenders on 6 May 1942; the Lingayen landing is on 9 January 1945; MacArthur announces the liberation of the Philippines on 5 July 1945
source: Cambridge University Press, Redemption (Invasion of Luzon); Wikipedia, Battle of Mindanao; EBSCO research starter on MacArthur's return
note: 8 December 1941 and 6 May 1942 are from memory; the 1945 dates were confirmed.

claim: Cebu is invaded on 10 April 1942; the Visayan-Mindanao force surrenders on 10 May 1942; Leyte is invaded on 20 October 1944; the Visayas are cleared by 20 April 1945
source: Wikipedia, Japanese invasion of Cebu (10 April 1942); the Philippine Diary Project
note: The 10 April landing is confirmed; the surrender on 10 May and the 20 April 1945 date (a round figure for the clearing of Panay, Cebu and Negros) are from memory.

claim: Davao is invaded on 20 December 1941; Zamboanga is landed on 10 March 1945
source: Pacific Wrecks (Davao, 20 December 1941); Wikipedia, Battle of Mindanao (Zamboanga, 10 March 1945)

claim: Dates for the Pacific islands, Burma, Malaya, Thailand and Indochina carried over from the year-end table of the earlier map (Tarawa 20 to 28 November 1943, Kwajalein 31 January 1944, Saipan 15 June 1944, Guam 10 August 1944, Peleliu 15 September 1944, Iwo Jima 19 February to 26 March 1945, Okinawa 1 April to 22 June 1945, the Japanese coup in Indochina on 9 March 1945, the fall of Rangoon on 8 March 1942 and its retaking on 3 May 1945)
source: From memory of the standard histories
note: Read each against a source before release. Where the earlier table gave only a year, the day here is a round figure.

claim: The borders between the new zones are straight lines in longitude and latitude, the nearest straight line to the province or front line each stands for; they are not surveyed borders
source: tools/split-pacific-zones.mjs (the reasons for each line are in its ZONES table)
note: The title of a zone says what it stands for (Hunan-Guangxi, Guangdong); Hong Kong lies outside every polygon because the outline data give it its own shape.
